isoDateTime.description: RFC 3339 / ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. The pattern enforces the encoding directly (the pinned ajv runs strict:true with no ajv-formats, so format:date-time is not used): a trailing Z is required and a local-timezone offset is forbidden. An optional fractional-second component is permitted because the orchestrator's terminalAt and recoveryHistory writers may or may not include millisecond precision.

overlayTierSnapshot.description: Snapshot of one overlay tier at run start. The sha256 hash is compared against the live overlay file's hash during --recover to surface drift in the recovery report. Each field is nullable because an unloaded tier records loaded:false with no path or hash.

recoveryHistoryEntry.description: One --recover invocation, appended atomically by recovery before the resume dispatch fires. fromStatus is recorded as a string rather than the status enum because the entry is informational rather than a re-entry discriminator and pre-revision runs may carry historic values.

terminalReasonCode.description: The 10-value terminal-outcome enum the orchestrator writes when the run ends. The enum is named here so the top-level terminalReason property and the allOf[0].then.terminalReason coupling both reference one source of truth — adding an 11th value is a one-line edit, and the test reads its positive-coverage roster from progressV1.definitions.terminalReasonCode.enum so drift between schema and test cannot ship green.

description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for the orchestrator-owned progress.json file under each run directory. The strict additionalProperties:false posture is load-bearing: any field the orchestrator writes that is not enumerated here fails validation, which is the reconciliation merge gate's mechanism. The schema includes the two E8-shipped writer fields (contractRevision, the failed-evaluation-rejected terminalReason value) so an E8-renegotiated run validates clean.

overlaysAtSnapshot.description: Per-tier overlay snapshot taken at run start. --recover compares the live overlay hashes against these to detect drift and surface it as a recovery-report warning.

recoveryHistory.description: Append-only log of --recover invocations against this run. Empty array on a fresh run; one entry per successful recovery thereafter.

runId.description: Run identifier in the framework's <YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>-<4 hex> form. The pattern is the contract: a value that does not match cannot be reconstituted into a run directory path by any framework code.

status.description: In-flight phase the resume dispatch reads at --recover time. Distinct from terminalReason: status is the coarse stage, terminalReason is the terminal outcome. complete and failed are end-state status values that pair with terminal:true.

workspace.description: Recorded workspace coordinates. F7's shipped recordWorkspace writes this at run start; --recover re-attaches the run to worktreePath, and --cleanup classifies teardown by createdByGan (a gan-created workspace is torn down, a user-owned workspace is left intact).

allOf.description: Cross-field invariant: terminal:true requires the full terminal triple. The writer contract O2 ACs 1, 2, 3 each describe the orchestrator writing terminal:true alongside a non-null terminalReason and a non-null terminalAt. The schema is the reconciliation gate; without this coupling a half-terminal record (terminal:true with null reason/time) would silently pass, which is the F5/R6 writer-vs-schema drift class the gate exists to catch.

Cross-field invariant: terminal:false requires both terminalReason and terminalAt to be null. This is the in-flight shape — any non-null value on either field while terminal is still false means a writer half-wrote a teardown.
